6.   Relegating this counter-argument to a footnote because I hate it: many people [say](https://x.com/Marxicology/status/2097719609067540910?s=20) “we shouldn’t worry about AI risk, because climate change (or AI misinformation, or some other thing) is more urgent and serious”. You simply do not have to choose: it is possible to worry about multiple risks at the same time.

[↩](https://www.seangoedecke.com/they-really-do-think-ai-might-kill-everyone/#fnref-6)
7.   Some people advocate for a “slow takeoff”. However, the main proponent of that view is Paul Christiano, who has [just today](https://paulfchristiano.substack.com/p/personal-statement-on-joining-the) joined OpenAI, citing “a meaningful risk that rapid acceleration in AI capabilities leads to catastrophic and irreversible loss of control in the very near term”.

[↩](https://www.seangoedecke.com/they-really-do-think-ai-might-kill-everyone/#fnref-7)
8.   This is kind of a Michael Huemer-ish [position](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethical_Intuitionism_(book)) in epistemology.

[↩](https://www.seangoedecke.com/they-really-do-think-ai-might-kill-everyone/#fnref-8)
